# ddot

> Computes the dot product of two double-precision floating-point vectors.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import ddot from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/ddot';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
ddot( N, x, strideX, y, strideY ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of indexed elements |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | First input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | `x` stride length |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Second input array |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | `y` stride length |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `number`: dot product

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
ddot.strided( N, x, strideX, offsetX, y, strideY, offsetY ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of indexed elements |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | First input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length for `x` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x` |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Second input array |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride length for `y` |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `y` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `number`: dot product

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `ddot()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`DDOT`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/ddot.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import ddot from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/ddot';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const x = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const y = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = ddot( N, x, 1, y, 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the strided interface:
out = ddot.strided( N, x, 1, 0, y, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `DDOT`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DDOT forms the dot product of two vectors. uses unrolled loops for increments equal to one.

### Further Details

jack dongarra, linpack, 3/11/78. modified 12/3/93, array(1) declarations changed to array(\*)

</section>
